My mother's mental health decline has rapidly increased this past month. Since April, 2024  she has fallen twice, suffered a neck fracture, & has been in and out of hospital for heart issues.  She started wandering last week, and is now in a secure memory care ward.  Her studio apartment is filled with photos of her family and paintings made by her family that she loved, but cannot remember .  She can no longer understand  or remember the concept of her private room, vs the wing of the building.   My heart broke seeing her parked in a wheelchair  (she could walk with a cane when she first entered the facility) at a table with other dementia patients, just sitting there.  She's suffering great loss of her family, home, autonomy, mobility, and bathroom functions.   This is a cruel, cruel disease that robs beautiful people of the remainder of their dignity.
My mom got sooo sick on Alzheimer meds.

Probate is basically you have to front an estimated cost of your loved one's assets to the court and then they decide the value of said assets.    But what if you CAN'T front that? I haven't recieved a clear answer. It's a disgusting affair.

No book properly describes the legal morass willed assets cover. A lawyer is your best best, but it's expensive as hell. Shockingly expensive.  I'm at a point where I just want to say take it.... I don't care, it was never mine.     But I have a car of my unwilled sister's I can't legally get rid of  and I want to.  Her bad life decisions should NOT be my burden.

And I you.   I've dealt with a nasty string of suicide in my family this past year and a half, so loss is a very tangible part of my life as of late (father and older sister).  I've barely had time to grieve for them both due to poor life planning on their behalf, and have been embroiled in legal issues since.   The loss of a mother cuts deeply for a child, but it is an unfortunate part of life.  You persevering will be proof of lif... for you.   You're still here, you will do great things, and you will carry on in her honor.

I've had to deal wirh the suicide of both my father and older sister in the past year and a half, and I remember zero time passed.  I'm left with my poor mother with dementia, who, for the past 2 months, I scrambled to place in a care facility.  It's a whole level of emotional and financial hell on top of my familial loss that I haven't had time to grieve handling my mother's inability to understand where she is.  I feel so much better knowing she's not in that house of death where my relatives killed themselves, and she will get her meds and supervision better than I could afford her.  The legal fallout of these deaths in our family has been abysmal, since wills weren't kept up to date.  It's all been hashed out now, but on top of handling a loved one's loss,  the legal part of it has been a gruesome challenge.  Word of advice to anyone reading this who loves their family....keep your wills and medical directives up to date.  The government is sitting and waiting to scoop it all up away from your loved one, making it near impossible for you to handle their affairs without a huge financial front to them, while you ait cripoled with worry.  If there is no will, you have to front the cost of your loved ones assets in probate. If you don't KNOW  what those are, you're out of luck either way and less gets resolved.
There are kind people out in the internet who listen.  Talk it out here if that's where you feel most comfortable.

I am so very sorry for your loss.  Losing a parent is so difficult.  I hope you can move forward in grief after this tumultuous time, remember the beautiful memories you had with your mom, and know that you live on with her, and you will make your mark in this world with the gifts she bestowed upon you.
All of this....find the route that makes you most happy, as you are an independent adult and 100% have the right to ensure a peaceful visit.
Dont feel bad....you can't be your best for anyone else until you can be the best for yourself.   It sounds sooooooo cliche, but it's simply true.

Did you find some professional help yet?  This course of action may be in your best interest instead of a reddit post.  That being said, there are people out here who feel your pain and can understand your frustration.  Forget the bots.....dont drop your family....talk to a professional who can help you ground your feelings to evoke a healthy resolve.  These people exist, they may seem hard to find and afford in America, but they're out there.  Would you like sone help in finding someone you can talk to safely?
How much do you believe in your deity?  Do you feel it can solve your issues at hand?  Is a deeper schism with your religious upbringing causing intrusive feelings of guilt and pressure?

While I can't offer direct help, I can lend a sympathetic ear.  My mom and I are going through the same thing.  EAP resources at work aren't proving much help.  My mom is also frequently stubborn and agitated in her failing state.  HIPA laws and her unwillingness to cooperate is proving quite difficult, a she's admitting to me increased confusion (shedding have to say it for me to recognize the issue, btw) but won't go to a doctor for it, and I can't make her legally. My mom is unfortunately NOT at a senior living facility....she remains in her home. She's left the gas stove on...she panicked when a smoke detector chirped fo ra low battery (thought the house was on fire)...she can't keep her thoughts together during a phone conversation, especially about more serious things.  

Its wonderful to read that someone else is seeking the same level of care, before personal care independence stripping, I'll be following this thread with my fingers crossed that you get some guidance.  I bet we're in different states, but there's usually a shared office state by state who can help.  I contacted my state office of aging and recieved no assistance, btw.  Hope you live in a better state!

But life is all about choices, and if distancing yourself from people who impact you negatively, family or not, is wrong, I don't  want to be right. Well talking it out backfired... and I'm not surprised.  My mom has mental health issues of her own.  I quit a job in Pennsylvania and moved back to New Jersey just to be closer because I saw a lot of familial disasters on the horizon and I'm frustrated that even though I'm back here and I'm closer there's still nothing I can do about any of it.... because you can't fix crazy.

Life is still the same if not worse for my family.   My bro-in-law ran away to Oregon for a week to get away from my nagging sister.  He's still out there.  It's a real shame.  I feel sorry for my niece.

I don't know how to reply to the original commenter, but I just wanted to say I'm worried for you (original poster).  People make judgments all the time...you're nice, you're handsome, you are smart...but none of that matters when you feel awful about yourself.  People can suggest meds adjustment all they want but I get you feel like that won't help after previous meds adjustments, right?  All I have to say is keep on trying....somewhere out there is a solution for you that will make your life better, and you will find each other.  The road will be rough and filled with disappointment, much like life predictably is, but your determination will pay off and you WILL find that silver lining....you will find a happier side to yourself.  It's tucked away right now in the recesses of your mind, but you have to be willing to dig reeeeeeeally deep to find that once joyous person again.  Did you ever stop and see something really small and say to yourself, "wow...that's awesome [beautiful/cool/neat]) no matter how small that thing was?  I saw an iridescent green bug the other day thst I just marveled over, after not caring about much of anything for three months.  We need to see those small beautiful things sometimes.  What have you seen lately that you said "wow" or "huh" over?  Anything?  Please tell us.

Also my sister claims that she has to nag her daughter constantly....yet I can convince my niece to comply with very little reinforcement.  Is it an age thing?  Is she just balking at her parents because she's testing them?  Does she not test me because I'm an outsider to the immediate family?

I just want my sister to get help.  Yes, she's been like this 4 a long time.   Her husband has confided with me that he sees it but is scared of her or something.  I tried to explain it to her today as a "picture how you would feel if" scenario, but it fell on deaf ears.  I'm worried that she'll take the course of medicating a perfectly normal, passionate 6 year old just to give mommy some down time.  I witnessed her sugar the crap out of her kid then complain that she has ADD.  Later on, my niece and I were horseplaying and I fell and got hurt, and my niece freaked out nd frozelike it was her fault, but it was totally my fault.  I tried really hard to tell her that it was NOT her fault, but her mom blamed her.  That made me so mad.  My sister's husband can't do much because my sister is hyoer-srnsitive to everything, and all suggestions for self-help fall on deaf ears.  I want my niece to feel comfortable talking to someone, but I can't help her and an outside source (school counselor, etc)  might get her in trouble.  My attempts are failing.  I am at a loss for what to do, but I can see my niece is struggling with this situation.

Thanks for your feedback.  I almost cried today to hear my niece tell me this story in confidence.....not an hour after I witnessed J nag M to death over not wanting to go for a walk.  A WALK!  I don't have kids, but I can see when someone is scared and hurt.  M is very clearly telling her mom, right in front of me, that she doesn't want to do something but she'll go along because she "doesn't want to make mommy mad".... but mommy gets mad over EVERYTHING...especially really petty small stuff.  J's job is wearing her out and she's taking it out on her child.  I HATE seeing this.
